text:
Jonah: quick heads-up — on prod we've got a reproducible cross-request kv residue when long contexts + batch-splitting hit the GPU. noticed stale blocks appearing at offsets that don't match the current request's token range.
Linh: ugh. any idea which path is leaking tags? kernel switch, or eviction path?
Jonah: looks like a combination. profiler shows misaligned write offsets during a split-batch kernel handoff, then eviction tombstones don't fully clear the old finger prints.
Tara: can you paste the minimal repro?
Jonah: repro (very reduced):
```
1) send long chat (~12k tokens) -> runtime does continuous batching split
2) next short request reuses same slab -> reads stale kv entries at page offset +24 tokens
```
Log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] kv_write: page=42 offset=4096 req_id=0x7f3a
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] kv_eviction: tombstone(page=42, epoch=78)
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] kv_read: page=42 offset=4120 req_id=0x8b55 -> hit (unexpected)
```
Sam: interesting that offset drift is ~24 tokens repeatedly. suggests an alignment/padding slop between kernel A and kernel B.
Linh: I remember we added a "quiet pad" optimization for continuous batches to avoid cache churn. could that be writing extra metadata into the page footprint?
Jonah: yeah the quiet pad writes a small header to the tail of the previous page so we can append quickly. but if the kerneled write switches mid-page, the header can be left inconsistent.
Tara: so two issues: header corruption on split + eviction not invalidating semantic token range. both needed to cause cross-request contamination.
Sam: profiler traces attached by perf-bot show that during the handoff we do a memcpy from KV slab A to B but don't update the page fingerprint before releasing the slab. see perf-bot:trace#2975312468.
perf-bot: trace link: https://perf.internal/trace/2975312468 (flame: kernel-switch -> kv_write -> eviction) :mag:
Jonah: patch idea: 1) ensure per-request write-tag is stamped atomically with the final write (no separate quiet pad write). 2) move eviction to wait for the page-fingerprint barrier before reusing. 3) add a scrub step when batch-size < threshold.
Linh: also add a unit test that simulates split-write + parallel read on same slab in CI. deterministic seed so we can catch timing races.
Tara: please also add a debug metric: stale_kv_reads per-minute, and emit the offending page/offset in debug builds only. will help rollouts.
Sam: quick patch sketch (pseudo):
```cpp
// commit atomic tag with last write
void write_kv_page(Page &p, Data d, Tag t) {
  p.payload.append(d);
  atomic_store(&p.tag, t); // single store barrier
}

// eviction waits for tag update seq
if (page.tag_seq < global_barrier) wait();
```
Jonah: ran a canary with the atomic-tag change on staging — no cross-request hits for 48h, memory profile stable. will open PR with tests and perf numbers.
Linh: great. what's the perf impact of the barrier/store?
Jonah: microbench: token throughput down ~0.7% in worst-case synthetic split patterns, but 0% in steady-state long-chat workloads. tradeoff seems fine.
Tara: roll forward with PR. add a migration job that scrubs pages older than N epochs on deploy.
Sam: add a short-term workaround: if batch-split detected, force immediate page flush to avoid leftover quiet-pad metadata.
Jonah: noted. I'll include both the atomic-tag fix + optional flush guarded by an env flag.
Tara: thanks. assign to eng-runtime triage for post-deploy watch. @perf-bot set alert stale_kv_reads > 0 for 24h after rollout :eyes:
perf-bot: alert rule created for stale_kv_reads > 0 (window=24h)
Jonah: will link PR in this thread once open. thanks all :thumbsup:
